pages.h1: Gentle Body Doubling for ADHD Minds
pages.intro: Getting started on a mundane or ambiguous task is often the hardest part of having ADHD. You declare one realistic priority, mute your microphone, and work side by side. It is a practical support technique, not a medical treatment, designed to reduce executive dysfunction.

sections.heading: Breaking Through Task Paralysis and Executive Dysfunction
sections.body:
Task initiation can feel like pushing through thick concrete when your brain struggles to find dopamine. When you sit down alone, a simple chore like sorting tax receipts or replying to a school email easily turns into three hours of aimless browser tabs and guilt. Having another person working quietly on camera changes the sensory environment in your room.

On {app}, you schedule a session that begins right on the hour or half hour. The simple act of showing up for another human creates an immediate external anchor. Instead of agonizing over where to begin, you narrow your focus to what you can realistically complete during a 25 or 50 minute block. You speak your intention out loud, set your timer, and let the quiet companionship pull you into motion without judgment.

sections.heading: Low-Pressure Sessions Built for Distraction-Prone Days
sections.body:
Traditional meetings demand continuous verbal energy, which drains an already fatigued executive system. {app} takes the opposite approach by keeping social demands minimal. Microphones stay muted after the brief initial greeting, meaning you do not have to make small talk or perform for anyone. The camera stays turned on, giving you just enough visual accountability to stay seated instead of wandering off to clean the kitchen.

If you find your attention drifting midway through, a quick glance at your screen reminds you that your partner is still working steadily. That visual cue brings your wandering thoughts back to your notebook or document. Because video is never recorded, you can work in comfort without worrying about privacy. If an urgent interruption happens, you simply update your partner in the chat box and return when you are ready.

When the closing chime sounds, you rejoin your partner for a sixty-second debrief where you report your outcome as done, partial, or not done. Marking a task as partial is treated as real, honest progress rather than failure.

Breaking large responsibilities into sequential 25 or 50 minute windows helps make time feel tangible. If you discover a coworking partner whose calm pacing matches your rhythm, you can save them as a favorite partner to book recurring sessions together. faq.q: Is body doubling a recognized medical treatment for ADHD?
faq.a: No. Body doubling is a behavioral support technique and coping strategy, not a medical treatment or therapy. It offers an external social anchor to help people with ADHD overcome task initiation hurdles and time blindness. You should continue working with qualified healthcare providers for diagnosis, medication management, and medical care.

faq.a: No. You only speak for a few seconds at the start to declare your task, and for a few seconds at the end to share your progress. During the working time, your microphone remains muted while your camera stays on so you both work in peaceful silence.

faq.a: Yes. Many people prop their phone or laptop on a counter to body double while folding laundry, washing dishes, packing boxes, or organizing closets. As long as you remain visible on camera, you can tackle physical household chores just as easily as desk tasks.
